name: npush
desc: Logic game similar to Sokoban and Boulder Dash
why: Sokoban and Boulder Dash style puzzler in the terminal, a classic genre that is worth a look but not unusual.

brief.what_it_is: nPush is a terminal logic puzzle game in the style of Sokoban and Boulder Dash, written in C++ and using the ncurses library for its interface. The player must collect all the gold on each level and reach the exit, with rocks standing in the way and dynamite available to blast them away. Unlike Sokoban-style games, the player can control several characters on screen at once. The README does not describe a file format for levels beyond saying players can send levels to the author.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes it as a logic game similar to Sokoban and Boulder Dash, with the difference that multiple player-controlled characters can be moved on the screen. The page also invites contributors who want practice on a simple C++ project.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the game internals are simple and structured so that a different front end, such as one using SDL, should not be hard to add. The interface is a terminal application built on ncurses. The README does not explain the puzzle mechanics in more detail.
brief.install_notes: The homepage names no install command. It says the last official release is in the download area and that the latest source can be fetched from the SVN trunk at https://npush.svn.sourceforge.net/svnroot/npush/trunk/. The homepage says the project needs ncurses for its interface. The SourceForge page lists Linux and BSD as operating systems. I did not see build steps, dependencies beyond ncurses, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: The main difference from classic Sokoban clones is that several player-controlled characters can be on the board and moved at once, which the author highlights as the core twist. It is a small, GPL-licensed C++ ncurses project with a deliberately simple codebase meant to be easy to read and extend.
brief.status: Quiet. The SourceForge project page marks it Beta, shows a last update of 2013-04-18, and was registered in 2008. The homepage still says iPhone and Android versions were planned for "this summer" with no year given, which suggests it has not been revisited for a while. I did not check the SVN repository for recent commits.
brief.caveats: The homepage's mobile-port plans are undated and no mobile version is mentioned elsewhere, so treat them as stale. The SVN link is the only route to the latest source and I could not confirm it is still live. The SourceForge page lists one user review (rated 5 of 5) and a 3 of 5 score for features. The brew description calls it a Sokoban and Boulder Dash style puzzler, which fits the homepage. The scout note calls the genre classic but not unusual, yet the multi-character mechanic is the feature the author stresses.
quotes: You need to collect all the gold on the level and reach the exit.
Main difference from Sokoban, KSokoban and similar games is that you can have multiple player-controlled characters you can move on the screen.
nPush is a terminal based application and uses nCurses library for user interface.
Have fun playing and make sure you send your levels in (my e-mail is in the readme.txt file).
